label: Week 37, 2026
recap:
This week was quiet for US AI policy, with 7 bill movements across four jurisdictions and no case updates or federal documents. United States Congress saw the most activity with 3 movements, followed by California with 2, and Michigan and Pennsylvania with 1 each. These figures describe changes in bill status, not passage of any legislation.

By theme, infrastructure and energy dominated the week with 4 bills touching on data centers, power draw, and the local costs of hosting them, including Pennsylvania HB2760. Children and minors appeared once, tied to United States Congress HB10315 on companion chatbots and protections for those under eighteen. Transparency and disclosure also appeared once, linked to California AB1405 on labeling AI-generated output. One bill did not fit any theme.

reading.body:
No bills moved, no cases advanced, and no federal documents were recorded in US AI policy between September 7 and 13, 2026.

The week produced no measurable activity across any tracked category: legislation, litigation, or federal agency action. This absence could reflect genuine lull, gaps in data collection, or the summer-fall transition typical in policy cycles. Without positive indicators of movement, the record shows only silence.

The lack of activity means nothing can be inferred about regulatory momentum, court precedent, or agency priorities during this period. This data documents what did not happen rather than what did.
